Summary: The first stable release of Rust, version 1.0, was published on May 15, 2015. This date is consistently mentioned across the sources, marking the milestone of Rust's first stable release. The sources also highlight that May 15, 2025, marks the 10-year anniversary of this release.

The first stable release, Rust 1.0, was published in May 2015. The project has been sponsored by the Rust Foundation since February 2021. It has been adopted by many software projects, especially web services and system software. It has been studied academically and has a growing community of developers.

## History [...] Work shifted from the OCaml compiler to a self-hosting compiler (i.e., written in Rust) targeting LLVM. The ownership system was in place by 2010. The Rust logo was developed in 2011 based on a bicycle chainring. The early 2010s witnessed increasing involvement from full-time engineers at Mozilla and open source contributors.

On January 20, 2012, Rust 0.1 became the first public release for Windows, Linux, and MacOS.

Summary: The first stable release of Rust, version 1.0.0, was published on May 15, 2015. This release marked the culmination of significant development efforts, with the vast majority of the standard library now stable and no longer possible to use unstable features with a stable build of the compiler. The release also saw many popular crates on crates.io working on the stable release channel and arithmetic on basic integer types now checking for overflow in debug builds.
